description: Curated subset of the research registry shown in the in-game equipment database. Only entries tied to systems the Moon tutorial currently represents are listed. Factual fields are copied from resources/research/nasa_technology_catalog.json by build_equipment_database.gd; game_usage is the only authored text and describes the game abstraction, never a real specification.

entries.game_usage: The tutorial outpost is a fictional starter habitat with nine compartments. It is explicit near-future fiction, not a reconstruction of a planned base.
The crew airlock uses a two-hatch interlock with a short pressure-matching step. It is a presentation abstraction: no gas mass, pumping energy or real procedure time is simulated.
Cabin pressure and gas partial pressures come from one well-mixed cabin model with finite stores. Rates, setpoints and alarm limits are tutorial assumptions.
Reference only. The tutorial habitat releases stored oxygen through a supply valve; electrolysis is not simulated and no oxygen is produced.
The CO2 removal device moves cabin CO2 into a finite captured store at a tutorial rate while powered and ventilated.
The water treatment device returns a configured fraction of wastewater to the potable store and sends the rest to reject. Purity and contaminant chemistry are not modelled.
The hygiene compartment records a wash routine and sealed-waste counter. Water used is moved to the wastewater store.
Delivered dry rations are a finite cargo reserve. Preparing a meal is a logged routine with a small water transfer; nutrition is not simulated.
Two growing trays need light, power, water, nutrients and cabin conditions. The growth time is deliberately compressed and portions are supplemental.
Inspiration for controlled-environment growth conditions. The game credits no oxygen from plants and does not model plant chemistry.
Solar generation is a configured available power multiplied by a sunlight fraction. No array geometry, dust or day-night cycle drives it.
The habitat battery stores energy in watt-hours with charge and discharge efficiencies and a reserve alarm. Values are tutorial assumptions.
A thermal loop and radiator device removes heat from the cabin heat ledger when powered. Its rating is a tutorial assumption.
A constant passive rejection term represents losses to the environment in the cabin heat ledger.
Flight-heritage reference for the astronaut's suit. Suit oxygen, power and cooling are not simulated in this build.
Lunar surface suit reference. The in-game suit is original artwork; no suit consumables or mobility limits are modelled.
Collecting a Lunar Sample is a single interaction near a sample marker. Tools and sampling procedure are not simulated.
The Equipment lock has a dust-removal station as an inspection point. Dust accumulation and removal are not simulated.
The outpost includes a protected shelter compartment. Radiation exposure and shielding performance are not simulated.
The exercise station records a timed routine in the activity log. No physiological effect is calculated.
Reference for the exercise routine. The game logs the activity only.
The sleeping quarters record a rest routine. Fatigue and sleep debt are not simulated.
The medical station records a powered inspection routine. No diagnosis or health value is produced.
The Science station runs a short powered examination of a carried Lunar Sample and records it in the activity log.
The examination preserves the sample in the inventory, reflecting curation rather than consumption.
The tutorial site is a fictional 40 x 40 cell lunar region. The mission perimeter is authored, not a computed suit range.
